name: GPS Spoofing and Telematics Manipulation
summary: The position or movement data a shipper relies on is deliberately falsified or suppressed, so that a vehicle appears to be somewhere it is not, or appears to be moving normally while it is stopped. The purpose is to remove the time window and location that any investigation would otherwise start from.
how_it_works: A jammer suppresses the satellite signal, or a spoofer transmits a false one that the receiver accepts as genuine.
Alternatively the telematics unit is physically disconnected, power-cycled, or its data connection is blocked.
The visibility platform either shows no update, an implausible position, or a plausible but false one.
Cargo is accessed while the record shows the vehicle in a benign location or in normal motion.
When the record resumes, the gap or the false track prevents the loss from being located in time or space.

indicators.signal: Position jumps a distance that could not be covered in the elapsed time
indicators.observable_in: Telematics track, tested for physical plausibility between consecutive fixes
indicators.notes: A simple speed-plausibility check between consecutive fixes catches most crude spoofing and is rarely implemented.

indicators.signal: Reported position is static or repeats identically while engine, odometer or fuel data indicate motion
indicators.observable_in: Cross-comparison of position against independent vehicle telemetry
indicators.notes: Cross-source contradiction is the most reliable detection available, because falsifying every channel consistently is difficult.

indicators.signal: Complete loss of signal in an area with no known coverage problem, particularly during a rest period
indicators.observable_in: Telematics gap analysis against known coverage

indicators.signal: Reported satellite count or signal quality drops abruptly to an implausible value while the vehicle is in open terrain
indicators.observable_in: Receiver diagnostic fields, where exposed by the platform

indicators.signal: Signal loss events recur on the same driver, vehicle or corridor segment rather than being distributed randomly
Telematics unit found disconnected, powered down, or physically shielded on inspection

false_positives.actually: Genuine coverage failure, tunnel or terrain shadowing, hardware fault, SIM or data plan failure, or regional interference not directed at this vehicle.
false_positives.how_to_rule_out: Check whether other vehicles in the same area and time lost signal too. Broad regional loss indicates environmental or infrastructure causes; an isolated single-vehicle gap does not.

false_positives.actually: Known receiver artefacts, cold-start errors, multipath in urban canyons, or platform data-processing lag.
false_positives.how_to_rule_out: Check whether the artefact appears across the fleet on the same hardware and firmware, which points to a technical rather than deliberate cause.

false_positives.actually: Documented wide-area interference affecting all users in a region, which is well reported in parts of Europe and is not aimed at any particular vehicle.
false_positives.how_to_rule_out: Compare against published interference monitoring for the region and period before drawing any conclusion about a specific movement.

preventive: Do not rely on a single position source. Combine satellite position with independent vehicle telemetry such as odometer, engine state or fuel, so that falsifying one channel produces a detectable contradiction.
Mount and wire telematics so that disconnection is not accessible without evident tampering, and alert on power loss.
Use tamper-evident sealing on the unit and include its integrity in the pre-departure check.
Fit independent trailer-side tracking on high-value movements so that tractor-side manipulation does not blind the whole movement.
detective: Run automated speed and distance plausibility checks between consecutive fixes and alert on physically impossible transitions.
Alert on any position gap above a defined duration, and treat gaps during rest periods as higher priority than gaps in motion.
Aggregate signal-loss events by driver, vehicle, corridor and hardware version to separate deliberate from technical causes.
Compare individual gaps against fleet-wide loss in the same area and window before escalating.
responsive: Inspect and photograph the telematics installation before the vehicle re-enters service, since physical evidence of tampering disappears quickly.
Preserve raw position and diagnostic data rather than the platform's cleaned track, because the artefacts that prove spoofing are usually removed by smoothing.
Reconstruct the movement from independent sources such as toll, fuel, weighbridge and access-control records.
Check published regional interference reporting for the period before attributing a gap to the driver.

regulatory_hooks.relevance: A documented risk analysis of direct suppliers must identify this pattern class where the carrier population plausibly exposes the company to it.
Preventive measures listed here are the kind of control a company is expected to define and evidence once the risk is identified.
